If you’re looking for a satisfying pure veg dining experience in Malad, Classic Pure Veg Restaurant is definitely worth a visit.

We kicked off the meal with a comforting **broccoli almond soup**—creamy, mildly nutty, and a perfect start. The **chef’s special pizza** was loaded with toppings and had a nicely baked crust, while the **paneer shole tikka** stood out with its smoky flavour and well-balanced spices.

Moving to mains, the **paneer char minar** was rich and indulgent, with soft paneer soaking up the gravy beautifully. The **veg Lakhnavi** brought in subtle, aromatic flavours, offering a nice contrast to the heavier dishes. One of the most fun and unique items was the **pav bhaji fondue**—creamy, cheesy, and super addictive with that classic Mumbai twist.

The **matka dum biryani** was a highlight—fragrant, well-layered, and served piping hot, making it both comforting and filling.

To end on a sweet note, the **gadbad ice cream** was delightful—loaded with textures, flavours, and just the right amount of indulgence.

Overall, a place that nails both variety and flavour. Great for family dinners or when you want to indulge in a hearty vegetarian feast!

From the refreshing mango pachadi to the subtly sweet notes in the curries, each bite struck a perfect balance between nostalgia and innovation. The rice paired effortlessly with the rich sambar and avial, while the crispy papadam added that much-needed crunch. And ending the meal with a luscious mango payasam was nothing short of indulgent.
The ambiance complemented the experience—simple, clean, and rooted in South Indian culture—allowing the food to truly shine. The staff was courteous and ensured everything was served fresh and on time, enhancing the overall dining experience.
If you’re looking to celebrate Vishu in an authentic yet slightly contemporary way, this mango sadya at Kamat Legacy, Malad is definitely worth experiencing.

featured_reviews.name: Manpreet Bhamra
featured_reviews.review_text:
For anyone who enjoys authentic south indian food, this is an okay place. Fair warning: food is strictly vegetarian.

Special thanks to our hosts for the evening Ms. Shivani and Mr. Raj for their hospitality. They helped us understand and pick dishes from the menu.

Kamat's Legacy serves unlimited Thali for lunch/dinner/breakfast. I tried the unlimited Thali for dinner but sadly it's not at par with other unlimited thali options that I have tried. The food is served hot and fresh but the amount and variety of dishes in are severely limited. Just about 4-5 dishes which includes the curries, no sambar or rasam are included which is really odd and the cost of this thali is ₹550 which is not justified.

Then comes the service: usually places offering unlimited thali (such as Maharaja Bhog or Jain Sabkuch) have an entire entourage of multiple servers constantly refilling your food without having to ask. There is no such system here. You have to request for refill every time and each time it takes them up to 5-10 minutes to get your dishes which breaks the tempo of eating.

I would rather prefer Jain Sabkuch or Maharajag Bhog if I really want to try the unlimited veg thali experience. Their service is top notch and the variety/amount of dishes offered is also better and at the same price as the unlimited thali served here.

We also ordered Bisi Bheli Bhaat and Podi Idli apart from the thali which were also disappointing. The quantity of food being served for the a la carte dishes doesn't justify the price of those items. For Podi Idli, we only got 3 medium sized idlis.

The quantity and quality of the food versus the price was a letdown which is why I don't really recommend this place that much. I also don't understand why there is an additional "service charge" included in our bill which is additional to the GST and CGST which we are already paying.

The only redeeming quality of our experience was the assortment of chutneys and pickles which is why I give it at least 2 stars.

We sincerely appreciate your comments about the service and the variety of dishes offered. We regret that your recent visit did not meet your expectations. We will certainly take your feedback into consideration to improve our thali offerings and the overall dining experience. We value your patronage and hope to have the opportunity to serve you better in the future.
Please Consider Your Ratings 2** to  5*****.

I tried the veg bao here for the very first time, and I completely fell for it. Soft, flavorful, and perfectly balanced, it instantly became one of my new favorites on the menu. The interiors deserve a special mention. The restaurant is very well maintained, clean, and thoughtfully designed. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, making it a comfortable place to dine in. After years of only ordering from here, it felt refreshing to finally sit inside and enjoy the cozy, well-kept environment.

The service by the waiters was equally impressive. They were polite, attentive, and genuinely helpful throughout the visit. From guiding us with the menu to serving quickly and courteously, they made the dining experience smooth and enjoyable.

What I loved the most was the consistency – even after a decade of ordering, the taste and service inside the restaurant matched the same high standards I’ve always received at home. That kind of reliability is rare, and Greens definitely stands out because of it.

Overall, Greens Veg Restaurant is more than just a reliable option for delivery – it’s a wonderful place to dine in as well. With great food variety, excellent service, and a clean, well-maintained ambiance, it remains one of the best vegetarian restaurants in Malad West.

featured_reviews.name: Ankeeta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience – Food Safety Ignored & Unprofessional Behaviour
This was my first and last experience with this restaurant, and unfortunately, it has been deeply disturbing—not just because of the food issue but because of how the staff and social media team handled it.
I ordered Davanagere Benne Masala Dosa from the Malad West outlet and found hard, crystal/plastic-like foreign particles inside the food while eating. This is a serious food safety and hygiene violation, not a minor complaint.
When I contacted the restaurant, one of the staff members assured me that they would help and specifically guided me to approach Zomato and also email them, stating that this was the correct process. I followed their instructions exactly. However, Zomato outright refused to help or issue a refund, despite clear photographic evidence.
What is truly shocking is what followed next.
When I went back to the restaurant team and their social media handles for support, instead of standing by their words or taking responsibility, they completely changed their attitude.
My comments explaining the issue were deleted from their social media pages
Messages were left unanswered
There was no follow-up, no accountability, and no resolution
This behaviour feels like a deliberate attempt to silence genuine complaints rather than address a serious concern. Saying “we are here to help” and then deleting comments and ignoring the customer is highly unprofessional, unethical, and misleading.
If this is how a restaurant reacts to a food contamination issue, it raises serious questions about their internal standards and customer ethics. Customers are not asking for favours—we are asking for basic food safety and honest accountability.
I am extremely disappointed with the staff’s behaviour and the way the social media team handled this matter. This review is being posted so other customers are aware of how genuine issues are treated once money has already been taken.
Food quality, customer trust, and transparency clearly need urgent attention here.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Customer,
This matter has been reviewed and addressed multiple times by our team.
The order was placed through a third-party delivery platform (Zomato). As per mandatory platform protocol, refunds can only be processed once a formal request is raised through the same platform. We had clearly and explicitly conveyed our willingness to approve the refund immediately upon receiving the official intimation from Zomato. However, to date, no such intimation has been received by us.
As part of our standard food-safety and quality-assurance procedures, we requested verification of the alleged foreign object. This request was declined from your end, making it impossible for us to validate the claim or initiate any corrective action.
Despite repeated communication and clear guidance on the appropriate resolution process, the matter has instead been escalated publicly across social media and review platforms. Such actions do not enable a fair, factual, or verifiable resolution.
We reiterate that we remain open to resolving this matter strictly through the appropriate and verifiable channel. Any further public allegations made without substantiation or cooperation will be duly noted.
We remain fully committed to hygiene, quality, and fair resolution for all our customers—something that is consistently reflected in our long-standing reputation and customer feedback to date.

Team,
Shree Gomateshwara Bhavan

We had last visited The Food Studio 2 years back m. Back then, we were served really good food, the place was jam packed and we had the time of our lives.

Having that fond memory, we decided to make a visit once more. We started off with a few drinks virgin guava Mary and scarlet sin ( pomegranate drink) both were quite underwhelming to be honest. In starters we ordered masala papad, cheese garlic naan, crispy chicken ,bbq chicken and chicken quesadillas. The cheese garlic naan was something that we had loved before, however this time around it was more naan and less cheese which was quite the opposite before. The crispy chicken was decent so was the bbq chicken. The chicken quesadillas were jam packed with corn unfortunately.

For mains we had chicken pad Thai and the food studio chicken pasta. Again decent.

In desserts we had a sizzling brownie and a kunafa, the kunafa felt more like a block of cream cheese covered with puff pastry

The point of this review being the place is losing its spark which is quite sad given the fact when it began, the food was literally chefs kiss. But now, not so much. It could be the fact that they have added so many things to the menu that the whole thing might be overwhelming the chefs. They need to rethink the menu is what I feel

featured_reviews.review_text:
During our recent lunch outing at Landmark Restaurant, Malad, we were pleasantly surprised by the overall experience, which combined great food, a warm ambience, and attentive service.

We walked in during the afternoon, and the restaurant immediately gave off a comfortable and inviting vibe. The interiors were neatly maintained, with enough space between tables to enjoy a relaxed meal. The staff welcomed us with courteous smiles and were proactive in guiding us through the menu. Being from North India, we were eager to try something that suited our palate. On the staff’s recommendation, we ordered Mix Veg Chingari along with Dal Makhani.

The Mix Veg Chingari turned out to be a delightful preparation – rich in flavor, with perfectly cooked vegetables that carried a smoky essence. It was a refreshing take on a classic dish and paired beautifully with the Indian breads we ordered. The Dal Makhani, a staple for us, was exactly how we love it – creamy, slow-cooked, and full of flavor, reminding us of authentic North Indian kitchens. Both dishes reflected the care and consistency of the kitchen.

The staff also recommended their dessert, Ras Madhuri, which we tried without much thought. This turned out to be the highlight of the meal – fresh, mildly sweet, and absolutely satisfying. It was the perfect end to an already fulfilling lunch.

We truly enjoyed ourselves and were so full that we didn’t feel the need for another meal until the evening. Overall, Landmark Restaurant delivered on every front – tasty food, clean and welcoming ambience, and excellent staff service. It is certainly a place worth revisiting and recommending to friends and family.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Hi Rajat, we're delighted you enjoyed your visit! Your kind words mean a lot. It's wonderful to hear that you appreciated the warm ambience and attentive service during your meal. The freshness of our ingredients plays a crucial role in creating delightful dishes like the Mix Veg Chingari and Dal Makhani, and it's great to know they met your expectations. It’s also fantastic that Ras Madhuri turned out to be the highlight of your meal! We look forward to welcoming you back for another delightful experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
🌿 Banana Leaf – A Slice of South India in Malad 🌿

If you’re looking for authentic South Indian vegetarian cuisine, Banana Leaf is easily one of the best in Malad. This place celebrates the flavors of the South with a menu that spans specialties from Andhra, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka — bringing the diversity of Southern kitchens onto your plate.

The variety is impressive: from crisp dosas, fluffy idlis, crunchy vadas, and hearty uttapams to full traditional meals. The highlight for me was their Dakshin Bhojanam Thali — a wholesome spread of curries paired with appam or parotta, with a choice of bisi bele bhath or steamed rice. Each bite was a journey through authentic regional flavors.

We also tried the Rasam Vada, and I must say — the rasam was outstanding. Honestly, I’d visit again just for that comforting, tangy-soulful bowl.

The ambience is cozy and minimalistic, enhanced by soft South Indian instrumental music and staff dressed in traditional attire — little touches that complete the cultural vibe. The service is warm, cordial, and attentive, making the whole experience even better.

💡 Verdict: A must-visit if you’re craving South Indian food — wholesome, authentic, and full of flavor. 🍛✨

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place on a weekend evening and was impressed by the beautiful South Indian–themed ambiance.
Valet parking is available, which is convenient. However, the service was quite disappointing—if you’re seated in the corner, it’s difficult to get attention, and we had to follow up multiple times for our order, which still took a long time to arrive.
The food itself was underwhelming; the sambar was very plain with no vegetables, and overall the taste and quality felt average, especially considering the service provided.
While the setting is nice, the experience could have been much better with improved food quality and quicker service.
